summary:
Technical health is good on hygiene and poor on scaling and durability. Strengths: no console errors in any run (the perf tour, smoke with warm-up, phrases and listen-and-do all on, 5 test files). Save loading is robust: 12 malformed or old saves all opened cleanly. eslint finds 0 undefined globals. JS heap is 4-15 MB. A save is 131 KB per slot after 90 simulated days. Boot is fast (title in ~0.2 s from file, ~70 ms of script).

Biggest weaknesses:
(1) Each frame re-asks "what's live?" through linear scans of chapters and hide-and-seek spots: about 28k CH.def calls and 120 SK.ready calls per frame. At 4x CPU throttling, zone maps run at 20-29 fps (31-49 ms per frame, of which tiles are only ~3.8 ms). With 3x the chapters, story lines and spots (a plausible 3-year buildout) a frame costs 500 ms at 4x and 97 ms with no throttling. A per-frame memo of 4 functions cuts frames 2.3-3.6x today.
(2) The only copy of the 3-year save is in Safari localStorage. There is no export or backup, no persist() call and no home-screen app, so Safari's 7-day storage deletion or a "clear website data" wipes it. A failed save is silent: stars were 37 in the game and 0 in storage.
(3) One exception anywhere in a talk freezes the map for good (verified), and one exception in a scene's update stops the game loop (verified). Errors are only written to the console, which nobody sees on an iPad.
(4) 36 wrapper layers over 22 functions depend on the order of the 56 script tags, and each new zone adds layers.
(5) Tests: the playthrough alone took 28 min (1684 s). The runner is serial and stops at the first failure, there is no CI, and timing flakes are patched with retries while the deterministic-clock hook in core.js goes unused. There is no performance, save-size, dist-build or exception-resilience test.

findings.title: Per-frame cost grows faster than linearly with content; zone maps already miss 60 fps at 4x CPU
findings.evidence: Chromium with CDP CPU throttling at 4x, real rAF loop, 5 s per scene (scratchpad/audit2/tech/out/perf-index-x4.json). Busiest maps, cost per rAF (avg/p95) and fps: juegos night 41.7/61.9 ms, 20.6 fps; abuelos night 40.8/60.5 ms, 20.9 fps; montana night 39.5 ms, 21.9 fps; bosque night 33.4 ms, 24.5 fps; villa 32 ms, 26.6 fps; playa night 29.7 ms, 28.9 fps; granja (barn) 14.3 ms, 52 fps. Split (split-x4.json): step() 0.6-0.9 ms, draw 31-49 ms, tile pass only 3.7 ms. CPU profile of juegos: seek.js 25.7% of samples (SK.ready 14.5%, SK.today 7.4%, SK.active 3.6%), chapters.js 14.3%. Calls per frame (counts.js): CH.def 17k-28k, CH.lineOf 8.6k-14k, CH.current 155-257, SK.ready 39-121, SK.hides 16-57. Causes: CH.def is a linear .find (src/chapters.js:71); CH.current, CH.lines and CH.next loop over every chapter calling it (:61, :62, :92-96); CH.alert calls lives() per person per frame (:233). SK.ready -> kindsMet filters 23 kinds x 43 spots (src/seek.js:71-72) and is reached per animal per frame via animals.js:574 hid(). Memoizing SK.ready/today/active and CH.current per frame, with CH.def from a Map (memo3.js, medians of 7 interleaved runs at 4x): villa 36.1->19.5 ms, juegos 42.4->15.1, abuelos 41.4->15.9, montana 39.7->15.4, bosque 34.3->14.8, playa 31.2->12.5, granja 15.5->9.6. Without throttling: 6-10 ms -> 2.3-4 ms. Scaling test (scale.js), 3x the chapters (36->108), story lines (6->18) and hide spots (43->129): 47.9 -> 500.6 ms per frame at 4x and 8.5 -> 96.9 ms with no throttling. With the memo: 16.9 -> 35.9 ms.
findings.impact: On a slower or older iPad the open-world maps already drop to about 20-29 fps. The 3-year buildout would make the game unplayable (about 2 fps at 4x, about 10 fps on a desktop CPU) before the content is half done. The same cost makes every browser test run slower and more timing-sensitive.
findings.fix: Step 1 (S): give chapters an id->def Map and a by-line index. Cache CH.lines, CH.current(line) and CH.lives() once per frame, or invalidate them only on quest or step changes. Cache SK.ready/today/active and kindsMet per zone per frame, and precompute spotsIn(zone). Step 2 (M): build one per-frame 'world context' (live chapters, favours, seek state) that NPC alert() and animal draws read, instead of each re-querying through wrapper chains. Step 3 (S): add a perf budget test that seeds a far-along game, sets CDP 4x throttling and fails if any zone map averages over 16 ms per frame, plus a synthetic 3x-content variant like scale.js.

findings.title: A 3-year save lives only in Safari localStorage: no backup, eviction risk, silent save failure
findings.evidence: Saves are one JSON value per slot in localStorage (src/state.js:90-166). No export or import, no navigator.storage.persist(), no IndexedDB (grep finds none). index.html has no manifest, service worker or apple-mobile-web-app-capable meta, so the iPad plays the site in Safari. WebKit's tracking prevention deletes all script-writable storage, localStorage included, for a site with no interaction in the last 7 days of Safari use. 'Clear History and Website Data' also wipes it. Storage-full test (savefull.js): the origin was filled to Chromium's measured cap of 5,242,857 chars, then a word was answered and +7 stars added. G.st.saveNow() returned false; the game had stars 37 and storage had stars 0; no toast; play went on in Field. tools/test-saves.js:354-358 asserts this silence as intended ('when storage fails, play goes on without errors'). No grown-ups screen shows the last save time or a failure. Saves on Windows (dist via file://) and on the iPad (GitHub Pages) are separate origins with no sync.
findings.impact: Over 3 years, a holiday break of 7+ days of Safari use without opening the game, a cleared Safari, a new iPad or a full origin silently erases the child's dog, words, album and learning history. That is the main source of motivation, and the parent's retention data goes with it.
findings.fix: (1) Grown-ups menu: 'Back up' exports the save as a file or text through the existing share sheet (dashboard.js and mictest.js already use navigator.share and the clipboard), and 'Restore' imports one. A weekly reminder in the parent dashboard if there is no backup. (2) Call navigator.storage.persist() and show the result. (3) Have saveNow failures set a flag; show 'Not saved since HH:MM' to grown-ups, and after N failures a gentle icon to the child. (4) Only after export exists, ship a home-screen PWA (manifest plus service worker): home-screen web apps don't count toward the 7-day deletion, but their storage is separate from Safari's, so the child's current save must move over by export and import.

findings.title: One exception anywhere in content freezes the map or the whole game; errors are invisible on the iPad
findings.evidence: Every map interaction runs inside the field's single long-lived playerWalk generator. It sets this.locked = true, then yield* interact/ev.run/fieldMenu, with no try/finally (src/field.js:95, 110, 114, 115). G.Tasks catches a throw, logs it and drops the whole task (src/core.js:164). Verified (softlock.js): Don Pepe's talk was made to throw. Afterwards field.locked stayed true, the field had 1 task instead of 2, held ArrowDown did not move the player and X (menu) did nothing. The only way out is a reload. The game loop (src/core.js:228-234) has no try/catch around step()/draw(), so a throw stops requestAnimationFrame for good. Verified (loopcrash.js): after one throw in Title.update, G.frame went from 33 to 34 in 1.5 s, a permanent freeze. There is no window.onerror. 22 console.error sites write to a console a parent never sees; only mic errors persist (mic.js M.errors, 10 entries).
findings.impact: Each new chapter, zone or favour adds generators that can throw, often on save shapes that only long play produces. For the child, a freeze looks like the game broke and ends the session. The developer gets no report.
findings.fix: Wrap interact/ev.run/fieldMenu calls in try/finally so locked is reset, and keep playerWalk alive by catching per interaction and continuing. Put try/catch around step() and draw() in loop() so requestAnimationFrame is always re-armed. As a watchdog, unlock the field if it stays locked with no other task and no scene on top for 3 s. Keep the last 20 runtime errors (message, stack head, scene, map, chapter step) in localStorage and show and share them from the grown-ups menu, like the mic test log. Add a test that injects a throwing talk and checks the player can walk again.

findings.title: Load-order wrapper chains (36 layers over 22 functions) are the structural cause of the cost and fragility
findings.evidence: Static scan (scratchpad/audit2/tech/scripts/wraps.js) found these functions captured and re-assigned. G.animals.tapped has 7 layers: errands.js, favores.js and all 5 zone files. G.zones.search has 5 (each zone). AN.update has 3 (juegos, abuelos, montana). G.errands.update has 2 (favores, connect), G.carry.tapSelf 2, G.st.playerSpec 2 (abuelos and montana clothing, each with its own memo), plus G.seek.tap, G.carry.drawHeld/show/plan, G.zones.drawUnder/dogReady/task, G.favores.alert/talk and G.words.meet. Every NPC's talk and alert is wrapped again at load time by connect.js (wrap, flag _post), phrases.js (_phr) and listen.js (_ld). Precedence is set only by the order of the 56 <script> tags in index.html. Each alert() per NPC per frame goes through connect -> phrases -> listen -> maps.js -> CH.alert, FV.alert and errands.alert. Globals: 152 top-level G.* assignments and 847 module functions on G.
findings.impact: Each new zone adds another layer to tapped, search and update, and each new system adds another NPC wrap. Debugging 'who answered this tap' means reading 7 files in load order. Reordering one script tag silently changes behavior. This is the main obstacle to growing the game safely over 3 years.
findings.fix: Replace capture-and-wrap with explicit registries before adding zones. For example: G.animals.onTap.push({map|zone, fn, priority}); G.zones.searchers keyed by map; an NPC pipeline G.npcTalk = [{id:'letters', when, run}, {id:'phrases',...}, {id:'listen',...}, {id:'story',...}] run in a declared priority order; alert() resolved once per frame into a cache that the field draw and the guide both read. Migrate one hook at a time, using the existing tests as the safety net.

findings.title: Save size grows with each word and is fully rewritten on every autosave
findings.evidence: 90 simulated days through the game's own APIs (save.js: G.words.meet/answerRight/answerWrong, G.st.said, G.hist, G.debug.dayShift, 40 retrievals/day, 15 min/day). Slot 1: day 10 29 KB; day 30 88 KB; day 60 122 KB; day 90 131 KB. Breakdown: words 82 KB (180 records, avg 446 B, max 490: 25 fields including ft with 12 date keys, due:null, learned, gold, mw); hist 40 KB, plateauing at 60 kept days x ~655 B/day (DEVLOG.md:126 says 'two months stay under 8 KB'); album 3.1 KB; phrases 2.9 KB; sayback 1.9 KB (one date per word, grows with words). Projection per slot: about 460 B/word + 45 KB, so 1,000 words is about 0.5 MB, 2,000 about 0.95 MB and 3,000 about 1.4 MB. Three slots at 2,000 words is about 2.9 MB, plus the mic-test log (up to 200 entries). The measured Chromium cap is 5.24M chars; WebKit's per-origin quota is about 5 MB and some versions count 2 bytes per char (about 2.6M chars), so measure it on the iPad. Each autosave (debounced 0.6 s, after every answer, talk and 15 s) runs JSON.stringify over all of G.state plus setItem: 0.43 ms at 180 words, 4.6 ms at 2,000 words; at 4x CPU 2.2 ms and 25.1 ms. Words of removed ids are kept forever (the unknownWord case kept 181 records).
findings.impact: Fine today. At the planned vocabulary, three siblings' slots can approach Safari's quota, which ends in the silent save failure above. Autosave becomes a dropped frame after every answer on a slow iPad.
findings.fix: Compact word records: drop default, null and derived fields (learned, gold, due:null, mw:[0,0]) and store ft as a short array; expect about 40% smaller. Split storage into keys per slot (words, hist, rest) and write only dirty parts, or move saves to IndexedDB with localStorage as a small index. Add a save-size budget test: 3,000 words x 365 days must stay under 1 MB per slot. Correct the 8 KB claim in DEVLOG.

findings.title: Test suite: 2h+ serial, timing flakes patched with retries, deterministic clock unused
findings.evidence: Measured wall time on this machine: test-choices 2 s, test-signs 5 s, test-learning 69 s, test-listen 70 s (160 checks), test-saves 71 s, smoke with WARMUP/PHRASES/LISTEN=1 137 s, test-playthrough 1684 s (28 min, 8 checks, plays c1-c21 over 5+ days). tools/test-all.sh runs all 31 files one after another with set -e, so it stops at the first failure and doesn't time each file. No CI (.github absent). Tests run the game in real time (G.speedMul 1). Under load the loop runs catch-up steps (at 4x, 94-121 of ~105-145 rAFs per 5 s did 2+ steps), so the world moves between harness actions. DEVLOG records 8 timing-flake fixes, mostly retries: 'tap again, up to three times' in tools/test-world.js:180 and tools/test-zone-playa.js:297, smoke's re-tap, test-chapters2's peek that 'flaked when several browser tests ran at once', test-ambient, test-review, and Tomás's road check. src/core.js:236 already has a manual-clock hook (location.hash '#test' skips the rAF loop) that no test uses.
findings.impact: A full regression costs over 2 hours of one person's machine, so it runs rarely and regressions surface late. Retries hide real timing bugs. With 3x content, the playthrough alone would take about 1.5 h.
findings.fix: (1) Harness: open index.html#test and advance frames from the test (G.step() x n, then G.drawFrame()). Waits become deterministic and can run faster than real time; per-step cost is only ~0.7 ms, draw is the expensive part. (2) Run files in parallel shards (4 cores; already 'two browsers at a time' by hand), print per-file times, collect all failures instead of set -e. (3) Split test-playthrough into per-chapter-range jobs that start from seeded saves. (4) Fixing the per-frame memo cuts frame cost 2-3x, which speeds every test directly.

findings.title: No tests for performance, long-play save size, the dist build or exception resilience
findings.evidence: About 1,630 runtime checks cover behavior well, but: no tool measures frame time (the 2.3-3.6x overhead in the first finding went unnoticed); save tests use hand-made small saves (test-saves SAVE() has 2 words), and no test plays 60+ simulated days and checks size; the harness only opens ../index.html (tools/harness.js URL), so nothing boots dist/club-de-espanol.html, the file the README recommends for offline use; nothing injects a throwing talk or scene; a corrupt slot is tested only as 'shows as empty'. dist is currently in sync (a rebuild in scratch was byte-identical).
findings.impact: The most likely 3-year failures (slowdown as content grows, an oversized or lost save, one bad content line freezing play, a broken single-file build) are exactly the ones the suite can't catch.
findings.fix: Add 4 small tests: test-perf.js (seeded far-along game, CDP 4x, all zone maps under a 16 ms average; plus a 3x synthetic-content variant), test-save-growth.js (save.js logic: 365 days, size budget per word and per slot, save time), dist boot (open dist and reach the title with no console errors), test-resilience.js (throwing talk -> player can walk; throwing draw -> loop alive; error log written).

findings.title: No offline play or real home-screen app on the iPad; the single-file dist parses 2x slower
findings.evidence: index.html has no manifest, service worker, apple-touch-icon or apple-mobile-web-app-capable. The README's 'dist ... works offline' holds for desktop file:// but not on iPad Safari, which can't open a local HTML file with scripts running. Load to the first title frame (load.js; local server, uncompressed 2.06 MB; GitHub Pages gzips to about 610 KB, so real transfer is about 3.4x smaller). file://: dist 233-251 ms, index 181-192 ms (59 requests). HTTP wifi: 741/762 ms. Emulated 4G (9 Mbps, 70 ms): 2.06/2.27 s cold, 0.23/0.19 s warm. 1.6 Mbps: 10.8/11.2 s. At 4x CPU: dist 1.46-1.53 s (script 438-446 ms) vs index 0.73 s (339-364 ms); warm 4G 0.98 s vs 0.65 s. JS heap at boot 4-5 MB.
findings.impact: No play in the car, on a flight or with bad wifi. On a slow connection a cold start takes several seconds of black screen. A home-screen icon opens a Safari tab with browser UI, which is easy for a 7-year-old to navigate away from.
findings.fix: After save export and import exists (see the save-durability finding), add a manifest (display: standalone, icons) and a small service worker that precaches index.html and the 56 hashed scripts (the build already stamps ?v= hashes) or the dist file, with cache-first and update-on-next-launch. Keep index.html as the GitHub Pages entry, since it parses faster than the single 2 MB file. Add a dark splash or a 'Cargando...' frame so a slow load isn't a black screen.

findings.title: Speech depends on device settings and the network, and is unverified in home-screen mode
findings.evidence: Recognition: webkitSpeechRecognition with es-MX (src/speech.js:159, 225; mic.js:26). On iPad it needs Siri & Dictation on (mictest.js:17 explains 'service-not-allowed') and a Spanish (Mexico) dictation language (:24). Windows Chrome's Web Speech recognition and Google TTS voices are server-based, so there is no mic or that voice offline. Whether webkitSpeechRecognition works in a standalone (home-screen) web app has not been tested on this iPad. The code already handles the known iOS quirks: starts inside the tap (gestureTap), resumes an 'interrupted' AudioContext and speechSynthesis (speech.js:178-195), primes the TTS (ui.js:240), keeps the last 10 mic errors and has a mic test with a share log. These are strengths.
findings.impact: Moving to a PWA or playing offline could quietly turn speaking (the strongest card growth) into '¡Otra vez!' every time, and nobody would notice except through a drop in the dashboard's 'said aloud' share.
findings.fix: Before any PWA switch, run the in-game mic test in standalone mode on the child's iPad and record the result in docs. Show 'Speaking: offline/unavailable' on the grown-ups Learning page when recent attempts are all errors (M.errors). Prefer local voices (localService) in G.currentVoice ranking so TTS works offline on Windows.

findings.title: Full-screen menus redraw the whole map underneath every frame
findings.evidence: Album, Notebook, Deck, ZoneDone and the field menu set transparent = true (src/album.js:41, src/menus.js:55/128/237/340, src/cards.js:331, src/connect.js:249/322). core.js draw() then renders the field, with its alert and seek logic, below them. Measured at 4x: album 34.8 ms/rAF (22.8 fps), notebook 34.4 ms (23.5 fps), deck 37.2 ms (21.1 fps), the same as the map itself, although they cover the screen.
findings.impact: Menus the child uses all the time (the deck, the album/Pokédex) feel as sluggish as the busiest map, and their cost grows with the world.
findings.fix: Mark the full-screen overlays opaque, or snapshot the field once into an offscreen canvas when the overlay opens and draw the snapshot dimmed.

findings.title: Canvas churn and the tile cache's wholesale clear will cause hitches as the world grows
findings.evidence: G.bigText makes a new canvas on every call (src/gfx.js:80-81). Measured: 60 canvases/s on the title, 120/s under ZoneDone, deck, album and notebook (cvstack.js: 1-2 per frame). Tiles are cached as 24x24 canvases and the whole cache is cleared at 8,000 entries (src/tiles.js:2341). A camera sweep of today's 21 maps created 3,752 canvases, so a 3x world will cross 8,000 and clear mid-play. A cold-cache first frame at 4x costs 120-350 ms (cold.js: villa 350, bosque 166, montana 162, playa 151, abuelos 138, juegos 121 ms vs 20-78 ms warm). Today the map-entry fade hides it; a mid-walk clear would not be hidden.
findings.impact: Small GC pressure today. Later, periodic 0.1-0.35 s freezes while walking on a slow iPad.
findings.fix: Cache bigText output by (text, scale, colours) in G.cached. Replace the clear-all with an LRU, or pre-render each map's static layer into one canvas per map and draw only animated tiles per frame.

findings.title: Dead engine code, legacy stubs and duplicated helpers
findings.evidence: The Embers of Aldmere battle sprites, src/sprites.js:237-1137 (63 KB, 3% of the bundle), are unused: G.battleSprite and G.weaponTip are never called. Songs battle, boss and sad in src/music.js are never played (maps use castle, church, field, headquarters, inn, story, title, town). 14 module functions are never referenced, among them story.js mamaIntro (a stub), errands.js tomasTired and urgent, chapters.js newRecent and tailStarted, tiles.js clearTileCache and drawMiniTile. 11 more are only used by tools/. Legacy stubs remain: E.unlocked and E.offer always return false (errands.js:57-58), D.legacyQuests has 13 ids, plus CH.tailGate and tailOrder. Duplicated helpers: isObj in 12 files, TT/T in 13, day in 8, ri/pick in 7, shuffle in 4. 15 modules each hold a lazy st() repairer for their slice of G.state, and there is no top-level save version. eslint: 17 unused variables, 0 undefined globals, 1 redeclare (G).
findings.impact: Small. It adds reading cost for whoever extends the game and about 65 KB of download.
findings.fix: Delete the battle sprite section and the unused songs. Move isObj, TT, today, shuffle, pick and say into one util module loaded after core.js. Add a top-level G.state.v and one migrate(v) function in state.js that the modules' st() repairers feed into. Remove the stubs once the child's save has migrated (chapters v3).

findings.title: An unreadable save slot shows as empty and can be overwritten with no recovery copy
findings.evidence: S.read returns null when JSON.parse fails or the shape is invalid (src/state.js:100-117), and the slot screen then shows '+ Nuevo'. Tested (save.js): a save truncated to 5,000 chars gave summary false and opened false, so the next tap on that card starts a new game in the slot and the raw text is lost. Other malformed cases (words as [], hist as a string, null records, bad seek/world/phrases/ch, future fields, a v0 errand save) all opened with 0 console errors. That robustness is a strength.
findings.impact: Rare, but a partial write or a hand-edited save would be destroyed by the next new game instead of being recoverable.
findings.fix: When a slot exists but can't be read, copy the raw string to spanishclub_slotN_bad before reusing the slot, and show a grown-ups-only 'damaged save' marker on the card (export available).
